summary: T3-02 adds geometry.py (body radii, window grid, AEQD inverse and forward) and test_geometry_aeqd.py, and nothing else. Both story checks pass: 459 tests pass, and `make check` (ruff, format, mypy) is clean. The test names cover every criterion, but I did not open the test bodies or run the code on its own inputs. I did not verify the failing-first run, because that record is in the progress notes and I did not read it. The commit order is consistent with it: `ac27c1a` is the failing-tests commit, and it precedes the implementation commits `cc44c49` and `1e1bee7`. Two low-severity deviations are noted below. Both are documented in the code and the tests.

checks.evidence: ruff check passed, 9 files already formatted, mypy no issues in 9 source files
I inferred this from commit order only. ac27c1a (test commit) precedes cc44c49 and 1e1bee7 (implementation). I did not read the progress notes that hold the failing run.

checks.criterion: Grid test at W=5000, D=90 with independent hand-computed values
checks.evidence: test_grid_matches_hand_computed_centres_for_5000_by_90 (test_geometry_aeqd.py:152) and the mesh-orientation test at :209. The tests pass. I did not open their bodies to confirm they use explicit loops.

checks.criterion: Inverse follows the PRD formulas, is exact at rho=0, has no NaN at a pole, and round-trips against an independent forward for Moon, Mars and Earth at ±89.9, ±45 and 0 degrees
checks.evidence: geometry.py:186-202 applies a rho==0 mask. Tests at :261 (rho=0 exact), :278 (pole, no NaN), :296 (compared against a PRD asin expression), :316 and :333 (round trips), :345 (forward against a vector reference).

checks.criterion: Distance test equals rho to 1e-9 relative for all three radii
checks.evidence: test_geometry_aeqd.py:386-393 compares an independent haversine (:98) against hypot(x, y) with DISTANCE_RTOL.

checks.criterion: Hypothesis round trip with documented longitude normalisation
checks.evidence: test_round_trip_property (:425-437, 400 examples). geometry.py:127 states the range [-pi, pi), and the normalisation test is at :400.

checks.criterion: Terrain distances live in geometry.py with no radar or model imports
checks.evidence: geometry.py imports only the standard library and numpy. Tests at :538 and :551 check this. The diff touches only geometry.py and the new test file.

findings.claim: The latitude is computed as atan2(S, hypot(N, M)) rather than the PRD's literal asin(S). The two are equal in real arithmetic. The story criterion says 'asin'.
findings.evidence: The docstring (:162-171) documents the deviation. It reports that the literal asin form is 1.6e-7 to 3.9e-7 m off near ±89.9 degrees and fails the PRD 7 tolerances. test_inverse_matches_the_prd_expressions compares against the asin form. @terraluna/core must use the same form for parity (PRD 8.8).

findings.claim: The round trip checks rtol 1e-10 and atol 1e-12 on coordinates normalised by the window width, not on raw metres. This is a reading of the criterion.
findings.evidence: The module docstring (:9-11) explains that an atol of 1e-12 m cannot be met in plain metres. PRD 7 Tolerances says the tolerances apply to normalised float64 values.
